title: Color Script
body:
Color Script is an ongoing painting practice in which color becomes an active force within a continuously unfolding pictorial world.

Rather than representing the visible world, the paintings construct temporary realities governed by relationships between autonomous color forms. Colors approach, overlap, resist, contain, interrupt, or remain indifferent to one another. Their meaning emerges through these encounters rather than from any fixed symbolism assigned to color itself.

A painting is never fully planned in advance. It develops through the act of painting. Forms emerge from the conditions already present in the work, gradually defining their own proportions, boundaries, and relationships. The image is discovered rather than designed.

The works often exist at the threshold between abstraction and recognition. They may suggest landscapes, horizons, architecture, or unfamiliar places without becoming representations of them. What appears is not a depiction of a specific place, but a temporary state within an imagined world.

Color Script is built on coexistence rather than assimilation. Color forms may intersect or penetrate one another while retaining their own identity. Interaction does not require one color to disappear into another. Instead, the painting develops through the changing relationships between independent elements.

Time is also part of color. A color that appears before another enters a different set of relationships from the same color appearing later. Each new element changes the field while carrying the history of what has already occurred.

Individual paintings remain autonomous, yet together they form fragments of a larger and continuously evolving world. Each work is both a complete pictorial event and one moment within a longer visual language.

Color Script does not illustrate predefined stories or symbols. It creates conditions in which color can act, interact, and form its own temporary order.

Painting becomes a record of these encounters.
